```{r shared-example, include=FALSE}
library(flashier.utils)
set.seed(17)
activity_truth <- cbind(
  c(rep(3, 12), rep(0.3, 12)),
  c(rep(0.3, 12), rep(3, 12))
) + matrix(runif(48, 0, 0.4), 24, 2)
effect_truth <- cbind(
  c(2, 1.7, 1.4, 1.1, -0.6, -1.2, rep(0.1, 6)),
  c(rep(-0.15, 6), 2, 1.7, 1.4, 1.1, -0.8, -1.2)
)
X <- tcrossprod(activity_truth, effect_truth) +
  matrix(rnorm(288, sd = 0.1), 24, 12)
dimnames(X) <- list(sprintf("s%02d", 1:24), sprintf("g%02d", 1:12))
fit <- flashier::flash(
  X, S = 0.1, var_type = NULL, greedy_Kmax = 2,
  ebnm_fn = list(ebnm::ebnm_point_exponential, ebnm::ebnm_normal),
  nullcheck = FALSE, backfit = TRUE, verbose = 0
)
view <- standardize_factors(
  fit, sample_side = "rows", scaling = "raw",
  prior_support = c(activity = "nonnegative", effects = "signed"),
  feature_scale = "simulated_intensity"
)
metadata <- data.frame(
  sample = rownames(X), group = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each = 8)
)
groups <- setNames(metadata$group, metadata$sample)
covariate <- setNames(seq(0, 1, length.out = nrow(X)), rownames(X))
```

```{r shared-checks, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(
  ncol(view$activity) >= 2, all(view$activity >= 0),
  any(view$effects < 0), any(view$effects > 0),
  identical(rownames(view$activity), metadata$sample),
  identical(names(groups), rownames(X)),
  identical(names(covariate), rownames(X)),
  all(rowSums(view$activity) > 0)
)
coordinates_before <- serialize(list(fit = fit, view = view), NULL)
```

## Native flashier {#native-flashier}

Native mean displays use per-component maximum-absolute scaling.
The scree plot shows native PVE.

## Shared setup {#shared-setup}

Run this setup once before a recipe. It uses 24 samples and 12 features.
Samples occupy rows. Nonnegative activity pairs with signed feature effects.
The group and covariate are artificial; no biological result follows.

```{r setup-recipe, ref.label='shared-example', eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
```

`scaling = "raw"`
keeps the native posterior-mean coordinates. Each recipe reuses `fit`, `view`,
`metadata`, `groups` and `covariate` without refitting or changing their values.

## Plotting recipes

### Factor variance {#recipe-native-scree}

Native PVE uses the fitted matrix. Nonorthogonal factors do not give an additive PCA variance partition.

```{r recipe-code-native-scree, ref.label='native-scree', eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
```

[Function reference: `flash_plot_scree()`](https://willwerscheid.github.io/flashier/reference/flash_plot_scree.html). [Shared setup](#shared-setup).

### Native heatmap {#recipe-native-heatmap}

For sample rows, `pm_which = "loadings"` selects samples. Native mean displays divide each component by its maximum absolute mean.

```{r recipe-code-native-heatmap, ref.label='native-heatmap', eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
```

[Function reference: `flash_plot_heatmap()`](https://willwerscheid.github.io/flashier/reference/flash_plot_heatmap.html). [Shared setup](#shared-setup).

### Native bars {#recipe-native-bar}

Each bar is one sample. Values are maximum-absolute-scaled posterior means, not raw activity or probabilities.

```{r recipe-code-native-bar, ref.label='native-bar', eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
```

[Function reference: `flash_plot_bar()`](https://willwerscheid.github.io/flashier/reference/flash_plot_bar.html). [Shared setup](#shared-setup).

### Native histogram {#recipe-native-histogram}

The bins summarize maximum-scaled posterior means. Group colors identify distributions; overlapping bins can hide one group.

```{r recipe-code-native-histogram, ref.label='native-histogram', eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
```

[Function reference: `flash_plot_histogram()`](https://willwerscheid.github.io/flashier/reference/flash_plot_histogram.html). [Shared setup](#shared-setup).

### Native scatter {#recipe-native-scatter}

The covariate is artificial and aligned to sample rows before plotting. The x-axis shows maximum-scaled posterior means; the y-axis shows that covariate. This display is descriptive.

```{r recipe-code-native-scatter, ref.label='native-scatter', eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
```

[Function reference: `flash_plot_scatter()`](https://willwerscheid.github.io/flashier/reference/flash_plot_scatter.html). [Shared setup](#shared-setup).

### Native structure {#recipe-native-structure}

Stacks use per-component maximum-absolute scaling. Their row totals need not equal one. Use nonnegative loadings; signed effects belong in a heatmap.

```{r recipe-code-native-structure, ref.label='native-structure', eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
```

[Function reference: `flash_plot_structure()`](https://willwerscheid.github.io/flashier/reference/flash_plot_structure.html). [Shared setup](#shared-setup).

### Activity heatmap {#recipe-activity-heatmap}

Colors show raw activity coordinates. No display normalization changes their values. Group labels describe simulated samples.

```{r recipe-code-activity-heatmap, ref.label='activity-heatmap', eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
```

[Function reference: `plot_factor_activity()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/flashier-utils/reference/plot_factor_activity.html). [Shared setup](#shared-setup).

### Activity points {#recipe-activity-point}

Each point is one simulated sample in raw activity coordinates. Overlapping points can hide samples; the example supplies no biological replication.

```{r recipe-code-activity-point, ref.label='activity-point', eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
```

[Function reference: `plot_factor_activity()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/flashier-utils/reference/plot_factor_activity.html). [Shared setup](#shared-setup).

### Activity boxplots {#recipe-activity-distribution}

`style = "distribution"` draws boxplots. Values retain raw activity units. The boxes do not show posterior uncertainty or a density estimate.

```{r recipe-code-activity-distribution, ref.label='activity-distribution', eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
```

[Function reference: `plot_factor_activity()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/flashier-utils/reference/plot_factor_activity.html). [Shared setup](#shared-setup).

### Activity structure {#recipe-activity-structure}

Nonnegative activities are divided by each sample's activity sum for display. This differs from native maximum-scaled stacks. Zero-sum samples are omitted. The plot records their IDs under `zero_activity_samples` in its `analysis_metadata` attribute. The checked example has none. Raw coordinates stay unchanged.

```{r recipe-code-activity-structure, ref.label='activity-structure', eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
```

[Function reference: `plot_factor_activity()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/flashier-utils/reference/plot_factor_activity.html). [Shared setup](#shared-setup).

### Feature heatmap {#recipe-feature-heatmap}

Colors show selected signed feature effects in the declared factor basis. With raw activity, matched effects reconstruct simulated intensity. No maximum scaling is applied.

```{r recipe-code-feature-heatmap, ref.label='feature-heatmap', eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
```

[Function reference: `plot_factor_features()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/flashier-utils/reference/plot_factor_features.html). [Shared setup](#shared-setup).

### Feature bars {#recipe-feature-bar}

Bars retain signed feature effects and a zero baseline. Selection uses the largest absolute effects per factor. Factor signs alone do not establish activation or repression.

```{r recipe-code-feature-bar, ref.label='feature-bar', eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
```

[Function reference: `plot_factor_features()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/flashier-utils/reference/plot_factor_features.html). [Shared setup](#shared-setup).

### Ranked weights {#recipe-feature-weights}

All features are ranked by signed effect within each factor; the labelled points are the largest absolute effects. Effects keep the declared coordinates. A label is a ranking, not a biological call.

```{r recipe-code-feature-weights, ref.label='feature-weights', eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
```

[Function reference: `plot_factor_weights()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/flashier-utils/reference/plot_factor_weights.html). [Shared setup](#shared-setup).

### Factor scatter {#recipe-activity-scatter}

Each point is one sample; axes are raw activity on two factors. Colour comes from the metadata column named in `color`. Co-occurrence across samples is descriptive.

```{r recipe-code-activity-scatter, ref.label='activity-scatter', eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
```

[Function reference: `plot_factor_scatter()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/flashier-utils/reference/plot_factor_scatter.html). [Shared setup](#shared-setup).

### PVE bars {#recipe-factor-pve}

Native PVE per factor as bars. Nonorthogonal factors do not partition variance additively, so bars need not sum to the total.

```{r recipe-code-factor-pve, ref.label='factor-pve', eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
```

[Function reference: `plot_factor_pve()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/flashier-utils/reference/plot_factor_pve.html). [Shared setup](#shared-setup).

### Data heatmap {#recipe-data-heatmap}

Observed values of the strongest F1 features, one column per sample ordered by F1 activity, split by group. Each feature is z-scored for display only; pass `scale = "none"` for supplied units.

```{r recipe-code-data-heatmap, ref.label='data-heatmap', eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
```

[Function reference: `plot_factor_data()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/flashier-utils/reference/plot_factor_data.html). [Shared setup](#shared-setup).

### Embedding {#recipe-activity-embedding}

Any named samples by two coordinate matrix works; here classical MDS of the activity matrix. Colour is raw activity per factor. Geometry is exploratory and is not batch correction or replication.

```{r recipe-code-activity-embedding, ref.label='activity-embedding', eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
```

[Function reference: `plot_factor_embedding()`](https://mdmanurung.github.io/flashier-utils/reference/plot_factor_embedding.html). [Shared setup](#shared-setup).

```{r gallery-checks, include=FALSE}
gallery_plots <- list(
  native_scree, native_heatmap, native_bar, native_histogram,
  native_scatter, native_structure, activity_heatmap, activity_point,
  activity_distribution, activity_structure, feature_heatmap, feature_bar,
  feature_weights, activity_scatter, factor_pve_plot, data_heatmap, activity_embedding
)
for (p in gallery_plots) {
  layers <- ggplot2::ggplot_build(p)$data
  stopifnot(length(layers) > 0, sum(vapply(layers, nrow, integer(1))) > 0)
  for (layer in layers) {
    for (axis in intersect(c("x", "y"), names(layer))) {
      stopifnot(all(is.finite(layer[[axis]])))
    }
  }
}
stopifnot(identical(
  coordinates_before, serialize(list(fit = fit, view = view), NULL)
))
```

## Next tasks

[Get started](https://mdmanurung.github.io/flashier-utils/articles/first-fit.html) explains native fitting and extraction.
[Advanced use](https://mdmanurung.github.io/flashier-utils/articles/advanced-use.html) covers units, uncertainty and membership filtering.
[Compare priors](https://mdmanurung.github.io/flashier-utils/articles/compare-priors.html) separates prediction from program recovery.
[Pancreas programs](https://mdmanurung.github.io/flashier-utils/articles/pancreas-programs.html) shows a real-data case study.
